subject: English Language
text: Choose the option that correctly completes the sentence: The basket of oranges ___ on the table.
explanation: The head noun of the subject is “basket”, which is singular. The prepositional phrase “of oranges” does not change the singular verb required.

subject: English Language
text: By the time the bus arrived, Musa ___ for nearly an hour.
explanation: The waiting happened before another past event, the bus arrival. The past perfect “had waited” correctly shows that earlier completed duration.

subject: English Language
text: She bought ___ umbrella because rain was beginning to fall.
explanation: “Umbrella” begins with a vowel sound, so the indefinite article “an” is required. The spelling and sound both support this choice.

subject: English Language
text: The students were congratulated ___ their excellent performance.
explanation: The normal collocation is “congratulate someone on something”. The preposition “on” introduces the achievement for which the students are praised.

subject: English Language
text: Each of the players brought ___ own water bottle.
explanation: With a singular distributive subject such as “each”, formal examination grammar uses a singular possessive pronoun: “his or her”.

subject: English Language
text: You have submitted the form, ___?
explanation: A positive present-perfect statement normally takes a negative tag. The auxiliary “have” is repeated in the tag, giving “haven’t you?”

subject: English Language
text: Ada said, “I am preparing for the test.” In reported speech, this becomes
options: Ada said that I am preparing for the test.
Ada says that she is preparing for the test.
Ada said that she was preparing for the test.
Ada said that she has prepared for the test.
explanation: When a present continuous statement is reported after a past reporting verb, it normally backshifts to past continuous and the pronoun changes to match Ada.

subject: English Language
text: The committee will announce the result tomorrow. The passive form is
options: The committee will be announced tomorrow.
The result will be announced tomorrow.
explanation: The object “the result” becomes the subject in the passive form. Future passive voice uses “will be” followed by the past participle “announced”.

subject: English Language
text: If the laboratory ___ properly equipped, the experiment would be easier.
explanation: The result clause uses “would be”, so this is a hypothetical conditional. Formal English uses “were” for all persons in this unreal condition.

subject: English Language
text: Select the word nearest in meaning to “cautious” as used in: A cautious driver checks both mirrors.
explanation: “Cautious” means careful to avoid danger or mistakes. In the context of driving, checking mirrors is an example of being careful.

subject: English Language
text: Select the word opposite in meaning to “scarce”.
explanation: “Scarce” describes something available in insufficient quantity. “Abundant” means present in large quantity, making it the direct opposite.

subject: English Language
text: If Chika says she will “turn over a new leaf”, she intends to
options: begin to behave in a better way
explanation: The idiom “turn over a new leaf” means to make a fresh start by changing one’s behaviour for the better.

subject: English Language
text: Which expression is most appropriate in a formal letter to a principal?
options: I would be grateful for your consideration.
Please sort this out for me.
explanation: Formal correspondence uses polite and respectful language. “I would be grateful for your consideration” states the request without sounding demanding.

subject: English Language
text: Which sentence is correctly punctuated?
options: After the meeting the secretary, filed the minutes. [comma separates subject and verb]
After the meeting, the secretary filed the minutes.
After, the meeting the secretary filed the minutes. [comma splits the introductory phrase]
After the meeting the, secretary filed the minutes. [comma separates modifier and noun]
explanation: An introductory phrase may be followed by a comma. No comma should separate the subject “the secretary” from its verb “filed”.

subject: English Language
text: Which sentence uses capital letters correctly?
options: Mrs bello travelled to kano in july. [all proper names uncapitalised]
Mrs Bello travelled to kano in July. [city name uncapitalised]
Mrs Bello travelled to Kano in July.
Mrs bello travelled to Kano in july. [title and month uncapitalised]
explanation: Names of people and places, as well as months, take capital letters. “Mrs”, “Bello”, “Kano”, and “July” are correctly capitalised.

subject: English Language
text: There are only ___ chairs left in the hall.
explanation: “Chairs” is a countable plural noun. “A few” is used with countable plurals, while “a little” and “much” are used with uncountable nouns.

subject: English Language
text: We have very ___ information about the new timetable.
explanation: “Information” is an uncountable noun in standard English. “Little” correctly modifies an uncountable quantity, whereas “few” modifies countable nouns.

subject: English Language
text: The match continued ___ the heavy rain.
explanation: “Despite” is a preposition meaning “in spite of” and can be followed by a noun phrase such as “the heavy rain”.

subject: English Language
text: Which sentence has the same meaning as: “No other runner was faster than Tunde”?
options: Tunde was a fast runner only.
Every runner was faster than Tunde.
Tunde was slower than all runners.
explanation: If no other runner was faster, Tunde had the highest speed among all the runners. The superlative form is therefore “the fastest runner”.

subject: English Language
text: Choose the correct word order: She wore a ___ dress.
explanation: English adjective order normally places opinion before size before colour. “Beautiful long blue dress” follows this standard order.

subject: English Language
text: The teacher spoke ___ so that everyone could understand.
explanation: The verb “spoke” needs an adverb to describe how the action was performed. “Clearly” is the correct adverbial form.

subject: English Language
text: In the sentence “The girl who won the prize is my cousin”, the words “who won the prize” form a
explanation: The clause begins with the relative pronoun “who” and gives extra information about “the girl”. It is therefore a relative clause.

subject: English Language
text: In the sentence “The new science teacher explained the rule patiently”, the subject is
explanation: The subject is the person or thing that performs the action. Here, “The new science teacher” performs the action “explained”.

subject: English Language
text: In “The coach gave the team a strategy”, the direct object is
explanation: The direct object is what was given, namely “a strategy”. “The team” receives it and is the indirect object.

subject: English Language
text: Neither the manager nor the workers ___ ready to leave.
explanation: With “neither … nor”, the verb agrees with the noun nearest to it. The nearer noun “workers” is plural, so “are” is correct.

subject: English Language
text: This route is ___ than the one we used yesterday.
explanation: A comparison between two routes requires the comparative form. The one-syllable adjective “short” takes “-er”, producing “shorter”.

subject: English Language
text: The prefect enjoys reading, debating, and ___.
explanation: Items in a series should have the same grammatical form. Since “reading” and “debating” are gerunds, “writing” completes the parallel structure.

subject: English Language
text: The principal asked the students to ___ their applications before Friday.
explanation: “Hand in” means submit a document or piece of work to an authority. The other phrasal verbs have different meanings.

subject: English Language
text: The doctor advised him to ___ attention to his diet.
explanation: The established collocation is “pay attention to”. English examinations frequently test such fixed word partnerships.

subject: English Language
text: In “They arrived early”, the word “early” functions as an
explanation: “Early” modifies the verb “arrived” by telling when they arrived. A word that modifies a verb is functioning as an adverb.

subject: English Language
text: Choose the correct word to complete: The farmer sold ___ produce at the market.
explanation: The blank needs a possessive determiner before “produce”. “His” shows that the produce belonged to the farmer; “he’s” means “he is”.

subject: English Language
text: Which sentence is correct?
options: The girl’s uniforms were neatly arranged. [singular possessive]
The girls uniforms were neatly arranged. [apostrophe omitted]
The girls’s uniforms were neatly arranged. [incorrect plural possessive]
The girls’ uniforms were neatly arranged.
explanation: The uniforms belong to more than one girl, so the plural possessive apostrophe comes after the final s: “girls’ uniforms”.

subject: English Language
text: Which sentence punctuates direct speech correctly?
options: “Please wait here”, the officer said. [comma outside closing quotation mark]
“Please wait here” the officer said. [reporting-clause comma omitted]
Please wait here,” the officer said. [opening quotation mark omitted]
explanation: In direct speech, the spoken words are enclosed in quotation marks and the comma before the reporting clause is placed inside the closing quotation mark.

subject: English Language
text: Which sentence is a polite request?
options: You will explain the last question.
Could you explain the last question, please?
Why have you explained the last question?
explanation: “Could you … please?” uses a modal question and politeness marker to make a courteous request rather than an order.

subject: English Language
text: In a formal report, “purchase” is preferred to
explanation: “Purchase” is a more formal equivalent of “buy”. The other options are also formal or specialised words and do not make the intended contrast.

subject: English Language
text: Which expression is most suitable in a friendly text message to a classmate?
options: I hereby acknowledge receipt of your message.
Kindly accept the assurances of my esteem.
explanation: A friendly text message normally uses simple, natural conversational language. The other options are excessively formal for a peer message.

subject: English Language
text: Read: “The library opened at eight, but the first readers arrived before half past eight.” What time did the first readers arrive?
explanation: The passage explicitly says the first readers arrived “before half past eight”. Half past eight is 8:30 a.m., so their arrival was earlier than 8:30.

subject: English Language
text: Read: “Although the road was wet, the driver reduced speed and reached home safely.” It can be inferred that the driver was
explanation: Reducing speed on a wet road is a safety precaution. This action supports the inference that the driver was careful.

subject: English Language
text: Read: “The notice urges students to return borrowed books by Monday.” The purpose of the notice is to
options: invite students to a sports event
explanation: The word “urges” and the return deadline show that the notice is a reminder intended to make students return borrowed books.

subject: English Language
text: In the expression “The wind whispered through the trees”, the figure of speech is
explanation: Whispering is a human action, but it is attributed to the wind. Giving human qualities to a non-human thing is personification.

subject: English Language
text: The statement “Her smile was like sunshine” contains a
explanation: A simile compares two unlike things using “like” or “as”. The word “like” explicitly compares the smile with sunshine.

subject: English Language
text: The sentence “What a wonderful effort you have made!” has an ___ tone.
explanation: The exclamation “What a wonderful effort” expresses praise and approval, so the speaker’s tone is admiring.

subject: English Language
text: Which word is normally stressed on the second syllable?
explanation: The usual spoken stress in “relax” falls on the second syllable. The other listed words normally take first-syllable stress.

subject: English Language
text: Which word contains the same vowel sound as “seat”?
explanation: “Seat” and “beat” contain the long /iː/ vowel sound. The other words contain different vowel sounds.

subject: English Language
text: Which word ends with a voiced consonant sound?
explanation: The final /g/ sound in “bag” is voiced because the vocal cords vibrate. The final sounds in “back”, “laugh”, and “leaf” are voiceless.

subject: English Language
text: A speaker usually uses a rising intonation at the end of a
explanation: English yes-or-no questions often have rising final intonation. Statements, commands and many wh-questions usually end with falling intonation.

subject: English Language
text: Choose the word that best completes: The chairman’s explanation was so ___ that everyone understood it.
explanation: After “was so”, the sentence needs an adjective describing “explanation”. “Clear” is the correct adjective form.

subject: English Language
text: The students could not attend the event because they had ___ the date.
explanation: After “had”, English requires the past participle. The past participle of “forget” is “forgotten”.

subject: English Language
text: The woman ___ handbag was found has been contacted.
explanation: “Whose” expresses possession and correctly links the handbag to the woman. “Who” and “whom” refer to people but do not show possession.

subject: English Language
text: Hardly had the lesson begun ___ the bell rang.
explanation: The fixed correlative expression is “hardly … when”. It shows that the bell rang almost immediately after the lesson began.

subject: English Language
text: It was the librarian ___ arranged the books.
explanation: The antecedent “the librarian” is a person functioning as the subject of “arranged”. The relative pronoun “who” is therefore correct.

subject: English Language
text: If I ___ enough money, I would buy a new dictionary.
explanation: The result clause “would buy” signals a hypothetical present condition. The if-clause therefore uses the simple past form “had”.

subject: English Language
text: The teacher explained that water ___ at 100 degrees Celsius.
explanation: A general scientific fact remains true regardless of the reporting verb’s tense. Therefore the simple present “boils” is retained.

subject: English Language
text: Choose the sentence without unnecessary repetition.
options: The final outcome result surprised everyone.
The final result outcome surprised everyone.
explanation: “Outcome” already means result, so adding “result” repeats the meaning. “The final outcome” is concise and grammatically complete.

subject: English Language
text: One of the boys ___ selected for the debate.
explanation: The subject is “one”, not “boys”. Since “one” is singular, the correct past-tense verb is “was”.

subject: English Language
text: The ___ of the new bridge was celebrated by the community.
explanation: The structure “The ___ of” requires a noun. “Completion” names the act or state of finishing the bridge.

subject: English Language
text: “Thank you for your assistance.” The most appropriate response is
explanation: “You are welcome” is the conventional courteous response to an expression of thanks. The other responses are not idiomatic English.

subject: English Language
text: The rain stopped; ___, the players returned to the field.
explanation: The second statement is the result of the first: because the rain stopped, the players returned. “Therefore” correctly signals this consequence.

subject: English Language
text: The news about the scholarship ___ encouraging.
explanation: Although “news” ends in s, it is treated as a singular uncountable noun. The singular past tense verb “was” is therefore required.

subject: English Language
text: Which word contains a silent initial consonant?
explanation: In “knock”, the initial letter k is not pronounced; the word begins with the /n/ sound. The other words pronounce their initial consonants.
